items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Benny Goodman gave him a clarinet at one time

ctx.x: Just took the name. Of course it was an honor for me to be named by Prez you know. He was such a great artist. He was a fantastic musician, not only a great tenor player and a stylist, he was a good musician. He played wonderful clarinet, but Benny Goodman gave him a clarinet at one time and we played a dance someplace and somebody stole it so he never did play it any more. He never played clarinet.
I’d heard that story but not the end of it. Too bad. When you were young—

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played with him a couple of times…did a concert at Lincoln Center with him just before he passed away, and it was great.

ctx.x: Well I guess I would be remiss in asking, do you have any Benny Goodman stories.

(laughs) No, I don’t have any Benny Goodman stories. I played with him a couple of times…did a concert at Lincoln Center with him just before he passed away, and it was great. I had a nice concert with him.
I remember that, he was in good form that night.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Benny Goodman gave Basie quite a few arrangements of Fletcher's.

ctx.x: And then there were arrangements coming out of the band.

Yes, yes. Buck was doing a lot of writing. We played a lot of arrangements of -- Benny Goodman gave Basie quite a few arrangements of Fletcher's. And that incurred more rehearsals, which we weren't used to, either.
Well, when did you start writing arrangements?
